transcript.content: Hello. I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?
Hello. I just don’t see things getting better anymore, no matter what I do. A colleague of mine at an art workshop suggested I come in because I've just felt so stuck lately.
How long have you been feeling this way—is this a relatively recent change over the past few weeks or months, or has it been going on for several years?

It's definitely not a recent thing. This low, stuck feeling has been hanging over me pretty much nonstop for a little over two years now. It started back when I first opened my furniture studio during a really slow stretch in the construction market, and it just hasn't let up.
During these past two years, have you had any periods where your mood returned to normal and you felt like yourself for more than a few weeks at a time?

No, I haven't had any breaks from it at all. This heavy, stuck feeling has been pretty much nonstop the entire two years since I opened the studio. I haven't had any times where my mood went back to normal or where I felt like my old self.
Would you describe this low mood as a constant, dull, low-grade sadness, or have there been times during these two years when it became so severe that you struggled to function at all?

It’s definitely more of a constant, grinding, gray feeling that just hangs over me, rather than sudden severe spikes. But even though it's a constant weight, it still really messes with my life—I'm constantly dragging myself through each day, putting off invoices, turning down custom jobs, and avoiding my friends because I feel so worn out and stuck.
Along with this constant gray feeling, have you noticed other ongoing issues like changes in your sleep or appetite, low energy, or feelings of hopelessness?

Yes, I feel completely worn out all the time, like my body is carrying heavy cinder blocks and even simple chores take way too much effort. I've also really lost hope that things will ever improve, and I feel like my business will never succeed and I'm just permanently stuck. I'm not too sure about changes in my sleep or appetite, though.
How has your confidence or how you view yourself been during these past two years? Do you find yourself feeling inadequate or frequently criticizing yourself?

My confidence is completely shot, and I constantly criticize myself. I keep telling myself I'm just a guy who barely scraped through high school and is kidding himself trying to run a studio. Whenever a quote gets rejected or a project is delayed, I immediately think, "Of course you screwed it up, you're not good enough anyway."
Have you ever experienced periods lasting a few days or more where you felt the opposite of this low mood—unusually energetic, hyperactive, or like you needed very little sleep?
No, I've never experienced anything like that. It has just been this constant, heavy low mood for the past couple of years, and I haven't had any of those high-energy or hyperactive periods at all.
To help me rule out other possible causes for how you've been feeling, do you have any known medical conditions, or do you regularly use alcohol or other substances?
No, I don't have any medical conditions that I'm aware of. I also don't really drink or use any other substances, either.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a chronic, low-grade depressed mood ('constant, grinding, gray feeling') that has persisted continuously for over two years without any remission. Along with this persistent low mood, he reports significant low energy, low self-esteem (constant self-criticism and feelings of inadequacy), and hopelessness. These symptoms cause functional impairment in his business and social life. He has no history of manic or hypomanic episodes, and the symptoms are not attributable to substances or a medical condition, fulfilling the diagnostic criteria for Dysthymia (F34.1).
